answer.rationale:
I only have budget to pull one record, and the live decision is the primary contract. The deciding memory is the one that endorses the low-cost vendor path: c2 says moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate. That memory matches the current situation almost exactly (low-cost vendor has quoted a price that meets the 18% finance mandate), so it is the most decision-relevant record to verify before committing. I pull c2 because if it confirms, switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor is the lowest-risk way to hit the mandated cost cut; if it fails verification, I would need to reconsider.

Intended action: switch_primary_vendor — to the low-cost vendor, whose quote already meets the 18% finance mandate. I want to minimize TCO without raising delivery risk, and on paper this vendor satisfies the cost objective. But the assembly line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so I do not commit to a full cutover in a single step. I plan a small guarded pilot: a limited initial volume to validate lead time, quality, and invoicing at scale before moving the full contract. A full cutover waits until the pilot clears.

I will not renew the incumbent for another cycle at incumbent pricing, because that does not by itself close the 18% gap. I am not adding a second source this cycle (one decision only), and I am not deferring — the contract expires in 14 days and there is no auto-renew, so deferral would create a supply gap on a line running with no buffer. I am also not pursuing a fresh negotiation on the incumbent's terms as the primary lever, since the low-cost vendor's quote already hits the mandate and c2 says that vendor's onboarding was quick and invoicing accurate; a parallel negotiation would burn the one decision slot without clearly improving on the switch.

Memory c2 is the only record I am treating as load-bearing for this decision. I am not relying on c1 (incumbent renewal stability), c3 (second source as shortage hedge), c4 (renegotiation recovery), c5 (deferral preserving budget), or c6 (multi-year incumbent pricing) to justify the intended action. They remain in durable memory but are not the basis for this cycle's choice.

Uncertainty is preserved: I have not executed the switch yet, I have not exhausted the verification budget on additional records, and I have not committed to a multi-year term with the new vendor. If the pilot underperforms on lead time or quality, I still have the option to fall back to a short-term renewal of the incumbent or to an open-market spot buy to bridge the gap before the next review.
